newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger confident of NZ government next week.
newsitem.headline: Bolger confident of NZ government next week.

text.p: New Zealand's caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday he was 90 percent confident the country would have a new government by the time parliament meets next week.
Bolger said parliament would convene next Thursday for the first time since an inconclusive election in October left the nationalist New Zealand First party holding the balance of power.

The date was effectively the latest allowed, giving politicians vital extra days to finalise coalition negotiations. Bolger's conservative National Party and centre-left Labour are both trying to form a government with NZ First's support.

"We're on the verge of a historic shift in terms of New Zealand politics, moving into the first coalition government," Bolger said. "We've been working on this now for seven weeks, why not spend an extra couple of days?"
He added: "We will have a government in New Zealand, I'm 90 percent certain, next week."
Bolger would not be drawn on concessions agreed by his party to NZ First, although he said his party's MPs had accepted them. "The explanations satisfied 95 percent of caucus," he said.
Bolger, prime minister since 1990, is fighting for his political survival in the drawn-out negotiations.
New Zealand First was initially seen as closer to Labour on social policy and issues relating to New Zealand's minority Maori community, but views Labour's planned spending as excessive.
Labour leader Helen Clark said she had called a special meeting of her MPs for Saturday to brief them on the state of the negotiations.
